### [FAIL] Cron comparison blocks rerunning the cutover after cron installation
category: logic
location: scripts/cutover_227_helpers.py:84-99

`production_changes` strips the new arguments only from the new file. After step 4 installs the cron file, a rerun reads that already-updated file as `old`. Its 17/main lines still carry `--url-key MT_TIMESCALE_MAINTENANCE_URL`, which the stripped new side no longer has, so step 4 reports a change and fails. The docstring's recovery path ("fix the cause, re-run the whole script") therefore fails for any later-step failure. The existing test only covers pre-227 to post-227, so the gap is untested. ### [FAIL] Health gate can pass on a stale log line
category: error-handling
location: scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:157-165

`run_health` calls `shell()`, which does not check the exit status, and discards the result. It then reads the last line of `backup-health.log` without checking that this invocation wrote it. Cron appends to that same log every 30 minutes, so if the step's own run dies before writing, a clean line from cron satisfies the gate. Fix: require the log to gain a new line during this call (compare the line count or timestamp before and after), and treat a non-zero exit with no fresh line as a failure.

### [FAIL] Host I/O errors skip the failure report
category: error-handling
location: scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:269-316

`run_steps` catches only `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`, so an `OSError` escapes and `main()` never writes the report. The module docstring (lines 4-6) promises the report is written on any failure. Realistic triggers exist: `arm.touch()` at line 188 can raise `PermissionError`, `step_offsite` runs `rclone` with `check=False` so a missing binary raises `FileNotFoundError`, and `step_production` reads `backup-health.log` at line 224 with no existence check. Fix: catch `OSError` in `run_steps` alongside the existing pair, and write the report even when an exception escapes.
